Observed multiple containers of cut vegetable to be cold holding with no date marking present. Discussed with PIC, vegetables were prepared yesterday (8/22/24). Date marking stickers were placed on vegetables, ensure any TCS food kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed the bar hand sink to be operating as a dump sink. Bar tender stated she uses the sink the kitchen to wash hands and normally operates this sink as a dump sink. Cease practice. Ensure bar hand sink is accessible during all hours of operation. Sink is a designated hand sink and should not be utilized as a dump sink. Discussed with PIC and bar tender. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

Observed no soap at the bar hand sink when Inspector attempted to wash hands. Discussed with bar tender. Bar tender stated she normally washes her hands at the kitchen hand sink. The bar hand sink was also being used as a dump sink. Ensure the bar hand sink is stocked with soap and paper towels. Cease utilizing as a dump sink. Hand sinks are for hand washing only. Discussed with PIC and bar tender. COS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed improper storage order in the walk-in cooler and the reach-in cooler near the ice machine. Walk-in cooler had Alfredo sauce and cooked sausage below raw ground beef. Raw shell eggs were above RTE salad material within the reach-in cooler. Ensure ready-to-eat (RTE) foods are above raw items such as beef and eggs. Items were moved below the RTE items. Ensure staff is aware of appropriate storage order procedures. COS. Discussed with PIC and employees.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the dish machine to have 0 ppm of bleach. Inspector tried multiple times and nothing registered on test strips. Facility PIC’s (both CFPM’s) attempted to correct dish machine so bleach was sanitizing correctly. Dish machine would not pull bleach to sanitize dishes. Dish machine is serviced by GFS. GFS was called during inspection to come repair the dish machine. Company will be at facility tomorrow morning. Inspector instructed the facility to either wash, rinse, sanitize in the 3 compartment sink (with bleach and/or sanitizer tablets) or wash and rinse in the dish machine and perform the sanitizing step in the 3 compartment sink. Inspector will follow-up on 3/8/23.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. Ice machine was observed with a heavy amount of mold debris - black and thick. Inspector shined flash light into the basin area and pointed it out to both CFPM’s. Bormida was called during the inspection to service the ice machine. Cease use of the machine until Bormida cleans the machine appropriately. Store bought, bagged ice was purchased until ice machine is serviced.
2. Soda gun nozzle was soiled with visible mold debris. Inspector showed the bar tender. Bar tender began to wash, rinse, and sanitize the soda gun. Ensure staff is aware to clean soda guns appropriately - wash, rinse, sanitize. COS.
3. All coolers were in need of cleaning: reach-in cooler near walk-in freezer (interior fan has dust, food splash on walls and base, food splash on grates), bottom prep cooler of cooler between both kitchen walk-in units (food splash on the base and grates, interior ledge lips - food splash), bottom pizza prep cooler (food splash on grates and base, exterior handle of the cooler - food splash), reach-in beer cooler at the bar (interior base has layer of black debris and mold). 
4. Walk-in cooler in kitchen has a layer of dust on the fan and ceiling - directly above the entire walk-in cooler. Ceiling and fan needs cleaned.
5. Shelving unit where the warmer is (next to rear kitchen hand sink and ice machine) needs cleaned of dust and debris - food is put under the warmer and clean utensils are on the remaining shelves. Clean all the equipment touching the shelving unit after washing, rinsing, and sanitizing the shelving unit itself.
6. Microwave was soiled with food splash.

Discussed the above food-contact areas in need of cleaning with PIC. Ensure staff is routinely cleaning the kitchen. Much of the above could be avoided if routine cleaning was happening more throughly at night in the Inspector’s opinion. Inspector will follow-up on 3/16/23 regarding the above areas in need of cleaning.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed almost all of the reach-in coolers and/or bottom prep coolers to have no thermometers available. Discussed with PIC. Keep extra thermometers on hand and replace as needed. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed in-use rags to be improperly utilized: facility is using spray bottles of sanitizer (quaternary ammonium) with rags. Cease practice. Rags need to be immersed in the sanitizer solution when not in use (with correct sanitizer concentrations) and/or paper towels should be used with spray bottles. Choose which method will work better for facility staff: sani buckets with in-use rags and/or spray bottles with disposable paper towels. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas where utensils were not being stored in a manner to keep utensils clean:
1. Pizza spatula and cutter observed soiled on the magnetic rack next to the pizza prep area. Inspector moved the items to the 3 compartment sink. Ensure staff is aware to not put dirty utensils back on the clean magnetic rack. Discussed with PIC. Repeat from last routine inspection on 9/9/22. 

Discussed with PIC’s. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. Ceiling in between front kitchen hand sink and reach-in cooler (before walking into walk-in freezer) has dust on tiles and vent.
2. Walk-in freezer fan has an accumulation of dust.
3. Food splash on walls: behind pizza prep cooler, behind pizza prep counter, behind all hot holding units.
4. Shelving above the pizza prep cooler area are soiled with spices and pizza dust.
5. Interior fryer is soiled with grease. Pizza oven directly next to the fryers has a layer of grease on side.
6. Metal cart used for chicken wing food prep needs power washed (employee stated bowels are rested on this cart) - heavily soiled with food debris and grease.
7. Hard water at the dish machine - machine needs de-limed and scrubbed with a stainless steel wool scrubber on the interior and interior door walls.
8. Top of dish machine has a heavy accumulation of food debris.
9. Most of the metal shelving throughout the kitchen needs power washed of food splash on legs.

Discussed routine cleaning of all non-food contact surfaces. Kitchen is in need of deep cleaning. Ensure deep cleaning occurs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Front kitchen hand sink (near walk-in freezer) needs re-caulked - missing and mostly gone.
2. Nudo board above the walk-in cooler and freezer is broken and coming away from the cooler units in multiple places. Material should be smooth and easily cleanable.
3. There is a tile on the wall where the pizza oven is - where the tile meets the Nudo board at the pizza prep counter - caulk to seal.
4. The shelf above the grill area needs caulked to the wall.
5. Mop sink is in need of re-caulking - black and moldy.
6. The dish machine/3 compartment sink area needs re-caulked - black and moldy. Caulk the entire area to the wall after removing old caulking.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs are corrected before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following physical facility areas in need of cleaning:
1. Walk-in freezer floors need cleaned (under shelving). Repeat since last routine inspection on 9/9/22.
2. Fryers and grill top equipment need pulled away from the wall - significant amount of cleaning needed behind the equipment due to food splash, grease, etc.
3. Both the walk-in cooler in the kitchen and the produce walk-in cooler outside need the flooring cleaned specifically under the shelving units.
4. Flooring under the dish machine/3 compartment sink area needs cleaned.
5. Bar area needs cleaned under the 3 compartment sink and hand sink - flooring has dirt and debris.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure the physical facility is cleaned as often as needed to prevent food splash, grease, and debris accumulation. Create a routine cleaning schedule to maintain the facility.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed multiple food handler’s licenses to be expired. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all employees re-take the food handler’s course and print certification for the facility. License is valid for 3 years. Ensure new hires complete food handler training within 30 days of employment. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed multiple allergen training certifications to be expired. Certification is valid for 3 years. Ensure all CFPM’s have allergen training certification and license remains valid. Discussed with PIC. Provided educational handout on how CFPM’s can re-take the course. Print certifications for the public health binder. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Both the can opener and the meat slicer in the kitchen area are observed soiled with food debris. The meat slicer was taken apart and cleaned. The can opener was moved to dish for cleaning. Both items were cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

The standing cooler next to the walk in freezer is observed with internal temperatures between 49F- 53F. Items of concern in this cooler are par-cooked chicken wings, chili, meat balls and hot dogs. During the initial observation (during the walk through), it was discussed that the par-cooked chicken wings had been placed in the cooler recently. Due to this inspector was willing to allow time to see if the foods would come back into temperature prior to the conclusion of the inspection. At the end of the inspection foods were still registering in the same temperature range. The meatball, hot dogs and chili were discarded during the inspection. As the chicken wings were still in their cooling process, and registering the correct time/temperature requirements, they were allowed to be placed in the walk in cooler to continue the cooling process. Inspector will be back to check on the cooler in a week to ensure proper cold holding temperatures are being maintained.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

1) The half pan used for storing the ice scoop for the ice machine is observed soiled and in need of cleaning. The scoop and pan were moved to dish for cleaning. 2) A pizza spatula and a knife are observed soiled and on the magnetic rack next to the pizza prep area. The top of the rack is also observed soiled. PIC consulted and instructed to ensure that the rack is maintained clean as well as ensure that only clean utensils are stored on the rack. The utensils were moved to dish and the rack cleaned/sanitized during the inspection to correct. 3) A cup of spoons next to the fountained drink machine is observed soiled both outside and inside the cup. Discussion with the PIC indicated that the spoons are used for tea by customers. The cup and spoons were moved to dish and cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

Single service sauce cups are in a plastic containers to the left of the steam wells used for cheese sauce. The container is soiled with food debris, a pen and a sharpie marker. PIC discarded the cups and moved the container to dish for cleaning. The writing instruments were placed in the adjacent bowl where they belong.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-501.14: WAREWASHING machine or other receptacles used for cleaning EQUIPMENT and other equipment used for drain boards shall be cleaned before use, throughout day to prevent recontamination as necessary, and at least every 24 hours. 

The dish machine is observed to not be draining in the middle of the cleaning/sanitizing cycle as it normally should. This is affecting the solution in the machine used for cleaning/sanitizing dishes. PIC investigated, and it appears that the drain was clogged. Once the items clogging the drain were removed the machine appears to be functioning correctly.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The caulking to the right of the dish machine is peeling off the metal sections that it is attached to. Caulking is also black to the point of being unlikely to be cleanable anymore. When discussing with the PIC it was indicated that this area was planned on having the caulking removed and redone in the near future. Ensure this is corrected prior to the next routine inspection. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Multiple locations through the facility are observed in need of cleaning: 1) the floor in the walk in freezer (specifically under the shelves); 2) the shelf over the steam wells holding cheese sauce and Italian beef; 3) the shelf above the pizza prep cooler; 4) the wall between the ovens and the pizza prep cooler; 5) the floor in the corner behind the meat slicer. PIC instructed to maintain the facility in a clean state.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The dish machine is not causing a color change on the inspector’s test strips. PIC was able to complete basic troubleshooting and provide 50 ppm solution during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Multiple locations noted during the inspection are in need of cleaning: 1) The rack used for trays to the left of the door as you enter the walk in cooler; 2) the floor under the shelves in the walk in freezer; 3) the holes in the non-slip mat in the dish machine area; 4) the shelves next to the hand washing station/ ice machine. PIC instructed to clean the areas regularly enough so as to prevent the accumulation of debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to run there hands under running water and then turn off the faucet prior to pulling a paper towel. Proper hand washing procedures were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that employees are using correct procedures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

The dish machine is not causing a color change obit he inspector’s test strips during the inspection. PIC contacted GFS for service during the inspection, but a technician would not be available while inspector is still present. Until service can be completed, PIC will use the dish machine for wash/ rinse cycles and then submerge dishes in a sanitizer solution in the three part sinks. Inspector will spot check Monday if PIC does not contact inspector tomorrow.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Multiple flies (6-8) are observed in the bar area around the three part sink. PIC stated that he needed to refill the fluid for the pest control devices and would do so. Inspector will follow up in 2 weeks for compliance. Facility should maintain equipment so as not to allow for the proliferation of pests.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

Aplastic cup is observed to the left of the pizza prep cooler partially drank. Cup does not have lid/ straw. Drink procedures and locations were discussed with the PIC and the cup was removed during the inspection to correct. Employee drinks should be consumed in a fashion so as not to potentially contaminate hands, foods or food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle of the soda gun in the bar area is observed with yellow slime. PIC is instructed to clean/ sanitize often enough to prevent accumulation. The item was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

1) A tub of cleaned/ sanitized utensils are observed across from the dish area in a tub that is soiled. 2) The half pan used for storing pizza spatulas by the hot holding service station is observed soiled. Utensils and tubs were moved to dish for cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

1) The microwave above the sandwich prep cooler is observed with accumulated grease and food debris. 2) The popcorn machine is observed with a thick accumulation of butter/ oil splash along the inner roof, the upper walls and the metal popper bucket. 3) The stand up cooler across from the ice machine has an accumulation of food debris in the bottom of the cooler section. PIC is instructed to clean the non-food contact surfaces in the facility often enough to prevent accumulation of food debris.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. 

The stand up cooler next to the walk in  freezer is observed with chicken at 48F and meatballs at 46F. The meatballs have been in the unit since yesterday at least. The chicken and meatballs were discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. 

Milk in the stand up cooler next to the office has been partially used and is without a date mark. Discussion with the PIC showed that the item was opened yesterday. Any TCS food should be marked with the date it is opened or the date when it should be discarded determined by date marking requirements. The milk was marked during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

A tub of cleaned/ sanitized utensils are observed in the dish area in a tub that is soiled. Utensils and tub were moved to dish for cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used

4-903.11: (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

Paper towels intended for hand washing are stored on a shelf under a wire shelf used for storing meals ready to be delivered to tables. The paper towels appear to have seasonings or food debris on them. PIC is instructed to store single use items in a location that will ensure no contamination from food sources, and ensure that they remain clean.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food should be maintained at 41°F, or less. findings.comment:

750-1100 Commercial dishwashing machines, dishwashing sinks, pot washing sinks, pre-rinse sinks, silverware sinks, bar sinks, soda fountain sinks, vegetable sinks, potato peelers, ice machines, steam tables, steam cookers, and other similar fixtures shall be connected in a manner that does not allow for backsiphonage or backflow into the equipment.

findings.comment:

findings.comment:

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
